summary: Reviewed the supplied manifest, business rule, production JavaScript, Python rebuild, rebuild tests, tie-out harness, report, and all local CSV extracts. The rebuild is materially independent of production, but I found one production-only rounding defect, one rebuild-only reset/return defect, and one tie-out validity hole that can let agreed wrong values pass as NetSuite matches.

independence.explanation: The Python rebuild appears written from the business rule rather than translated from production: it sorts by transaction date plus business event order, handles zero-quantity value rows, and keeps Decimal cent rounding, while production sorts only by created timestamp, skips zero-quantity rows, and uses JavaScript Number/Math.round.

findings.claim: Production rounds negative outbound value changes with JavaScript Math.round, which rounds half-cent negative values toward zero instead of to the cent implied by the rebuild/business-rule tests.
findings.scenario: Rows in order: id 1 ItemRcpt item X location L trandate 2026-03-01 created 09:00 quantity 2 amount 2.01, then id 2 ItemShip trandate 2026-03-02 created 09:00 quantity -1. Running average before the shipment is 1.005; the shipment should remove 1.01 and leave qty 1 value 1.00, but production computes about -1.00 and leaves value 1.01.
findings.test_to_confirm: Add events [{id:1,type:ItemRcpt,item:X,location:L,trandate:2026-03-01,created:2026-03-01T09:00:00,quantity:2,amount:2.01},{id:2,type:ItemShip,item:X,location:L,trandate:2026-03-02,created:2026-03-02T09:00:00,quantity:-1,amount:""}]. Expected ending pool X/L: qty 1, value 1.00.

findings.claim: The rebuild keeps a hidden last average after the pool resets to zero, so a later customer return is valued from the old depleted pool instead of the reset pool.
findings.scenario: Rows in order: id 1 ItemRcpt item X location L quantity 10 amount 100.00, id 2 ItemShip quantity -10, id 3 RtnAuth quantity 2. After id 2 the business rule says the pool resets to 0 value; the next return has no positive running pool and should come in at 0.00 value, but rebuild uses the prior 10.00 average and returns qty 2 value 20.00.
findings.test_to_confirm: Add events [{id:1,type:ItemRcpt,item:X,location:L,trandate:2026-03-01,created:2026-03-01T09:00:00,quantity:10,amount:100.00},{id:2,type:ItemShip,item:X,location:L,trandate:2026-03-02,created:2026-03-02T09:00:00,quantity:-10,amount:""},{id:3,type:RtnAuth,item:X,location:L,trandate:2026-03-03,created:2026-03-03T09:00:00,quantity:2,amount:""}]. Expected ending pool X/L under reset semantics: qty 2, value 0.00.

findings.claim: The tie-out can mark a pool as matched when quantity and average are within tolerance even though the actual on-hand value differs by more than a cent.
findings.scenario: For one pool X/L, rebuild and production both produce qty 100000 value 1000000.00, so avg 10.00000. NetSuite aggregateitemlocation has quantityonhand 100000, averagecost 10.00049, onhandvalue 1000049.00. The tie-out condition accepts the pool because average difference 0.00049 is within AVG_TOL, yet the reported value is wrong by 49.00.
findings.test_to_confirm: Use a netsuite_aggregateitemlocation row item X location L quantityonhand 100000 averagecost 10.00049 onhandvalue 1000049.00 and rebuild pool qty 100000 value 1000000.00. Expected tie-out result: UNMATCHED because onhandvalue differs by 49.00, even though average is within 0.0005.
